summary: Customers can upload files when submitting a support ticket.

threats.title: Malicious file upload bypasses validation
threats.scenario: An attacker uploads a crafted file that bypasses content-type or extension checks and is later processed by downstream systems.
threats.impact: Malware delivery, downstream processing compromise, or stored malicious content.
mitigations: Validate file type server-side using magic bytes, not just extension
Scan all uploads with malware detection before processing
Store files outside direct web root with no direct URL access
Generate random object names to prevent enumeration
assumptions: The feature supports user-supplied file uploads
Files are stored in S3 or similar object storage

threats.title: Unauthorized access to uploaded files
threats.scenario: A user guesses or reuses file URLs and accesses attachments belonging to another customer.
threats.impact: Exposure of PII or sensitive support content.
mitigations: Enforce object-level authorization on every download request
Avoid predictable object identifiers in URLs
Log and alert on repeated access failures
assumptions: Attachments can be retrieved after upload
Files are accessible via direct URL

abuse_cases: Upload malware disguised as a document (e.g., .exe renamed to .pdf)
Attempt IDOR against attachment download endpoints to access other users' files
security_questions: Are uploads scanned synchronously or asynchronously?
Are attachments ever rendered inline in the browser?
What file types and size limits are allowed?
